docs.title: Introduction
docs.desc: vinland-ui is a utility-first UI framework for Odin. You write UI in Odin, style it with Tailwind-style classes that resolve through design tokens, and a GPU renderer draws it at your display's real pixel density.

blocks.text: vinland-ui is a utility-first UI framework for Odin. You write UI in Odin, style it with Tailwind-style classes that resolve through design tokens, and a GPU renderer draws it at your display's real pixel density.
What it is

A small set of Odin packages. `vui` holds the element tree, the utility parser, design tokens, layout, text shaping and painting. `vui/app` is a host built on SDL3 GPU (Metal on macOS, Vulkan on Linux) with an OpenGL 3.3 fallback that owns the window, input and the control server. `vui/fonts` embeds Inter, IBM Plex Mono and Source Serif 4, and `vui/icons` ships Heroicons.
The core never draws anything on its own. A `ui.div` is an empty box until you give it classes, so the look of an app lives entirely in your code and in your theme.
How it reads

Containers open with `if ui.div("...") { }` and close automatically at the end of the block. Leaves such as `ui.text`, `ui.icon` and `ui.el` take a class string. Interaction is queried where you build: `ui.clicked()`, `ui.hovered()` and friends refer to the element you are inside.
Inspiration

Jetpack Compose showed that UI can live in the host language. Flutter showed the value of owning the renderer end to end. Quickshell showed how good small desktop widgets can feel when animation is cheap. Tailwind CSS supplied the vocabulary: if you know Tailwind, you already know how to style vinland-ui.

docs.title: Installation
docs.desc: Add vinland-ui to an Odin project and open your first window.

blocks.text: Add vinland-ui to an Odin project and open your first window.
Requirements
Odin (dev-2026-11 or newer), SDL3 development files, and Metal (macOS) or Vulkan (Linux) with automatic OpenGL 3.3 fallback. Fonts and icons are embedded, so there is nothing else to install.

blocks.code:
# macOS
brew install odin sdl3
# Arch
sudo pacman -S sdl3
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install libsdl3-dev

blocks.text: Add the packages
Clone the repository next to your project (or as a git submodule) and import the packages by path, or register a collection with `-collection:vinland=path/to/vinland-ui`.

blocks.code:
git clone https://github.com/WilsonNet/vinland-ui
odin build my_app -collection:vinland=vinland-ui

blocks.text: A first window
Bring your own renderer

Games that already own a render loop (raylib, Vulkan, Metal, a custom engine) can skip `vui/app`: call `ui.begin_frame` with your input, build, call `ui.end_frame` and draw the returned `Draw_List`. Each command is one instanced quad; `vui/app/shaders/` (GLSL and MSL) and `vui/app/gl.odin` are the reference implementations of the uber-shader.

docs.title: Agent skill & CLI
docs.desc: Drive a running app from the terminal: navigate, click, type, and take screenshots. Built for AI agents and tests.

blocks.text: Drive a running app from the terminal: navigate, click, type, and take screenshots. Built for AI agents and tests.
Every vinland-ui app can expose a local control port. `vui-ctl` speaks to it, which gives agents and tests the same feedback loop a person gets from looking at the screen.
Run an app headless

blocks.code:
# render offscreen at a fixed scale; nothing appears on your desktop
VUI_HIDDEN=1 VUI_SCALE=2 VUI_SIZE=1440x900 ./build/showroom &

./build/vui-ctl info
./build/vui-ctl nav page=box-shadow
./build/vui-ctl dark on
./build/vui-ctl screenshot shadow-dark.png
./build/vui-ctl click-text "Show all"
./build/vui-ctl scroll 600
./build/vui-ctl tree 6 | jq '.nodes[] | select(.t)'

blocks.text: Drive a visible app without stealing input

Pointer and key commands are injected inside the app: they never warp or click the real OS pointer, raise the window or request focus. When the window should stay visible while someone else uses the machine, start it with `VUI_BACKGROUND=1`. It is mapped without activation and with the non-focusable hint (plus `SDL_MAC_BACKGROUND_APP=1` on macOS so no Dock icon or focus steal occurs), so a game or editor normally keeps keyboard and pointer focus. X11 window managers and macOS honor the hints; Wayland leaves focus policy to the compositor, where a no-focus rule is the reliable option.

blocks.code:
VUI_BACKGROUND=1 VUI_PORT=7420 ./build/my_app &
./build/vui-ctl info          # background:true, focusable:false, keyboard_focus:false
./build/vui-ctl click-text "Save"
./build/vui-ctl foreground    # escape hatch: native dialog, IME, human takeover
./build/vui-ctl background    # back to non-focusable driving

blocks.text: A compositor may refuse to make an existing Wayland surface focusable; the foreground response reports that, and restarting without `VUI_BACKGROUND=1` is the fallback for flows that need native focus.
Commands

rows: viewport, scale, frame time, backend/driver, focus state, node count, unknown classes
clicks the element whose text matches
opt into OS focus / return to non-focusable driving
drop a stuck synthetic button or drag
element tree with rects, classes and text as JSON

blocks.text: Agent skill

The repository ships `skills/vinland-ui/SKILL.md` (symlinked at `.agents/skills/vinland-ui` for automatic agent discovery). It teaches the element API, the utility vocabulary, the token system and this CLI loop, so an agent can build a screen, screenshot it and iterate without a human in the loop.

docs.title: Testing
docs.desc: Playwright-style end-to-end tests for native apps: click by text, assert on the element tree, diff screenshots against baselines. Headless runs are sandboxed.

blocks.text: Playwright-style end-to-end tests for native apps: click by text, assert on the element tree, diff screenshots against baselines. Headless runs are sandboxed.

`vui-test` runs end-to-end suites against a real vinland-ui app, the way Playwright tests a web app: it launches the binary, clicks and types by visible text, asserts on the element tree, and compares screenshots with committed baselines. The app is driven over the same control port `vui-ctl` uses, so a test exercises the shipping build with no test hooks compiled in.

blocks.code:
# tests/e2e/showroom.vt
app ../../build/showroom
size 1280x800
baselines baselines

test "navigate to canvas page"
  click "Canvas & charts"
  expect-text "Drawing primitives"
  expect-class "Canvas & charts" text-accent
  expect-frame-ms 40
  screenshot canvas

blocks.text: Writing a suite

A suite is a plain text file with one directive per line. Arguments with spaces go in double quotes, and `#` starts a comment. Directives at the top configure the app; each `test "name"` starts a test whose steps follow, indented or not.

rows: executable and arguments, relative to cwd
working directory, relative to the suite file
baseline screenshot directory, relative to the suite

blocks.text: The `app` line and `env` values expand `{out}` (the output directory), `{dir}` (the suite directory) and `{test}` (a scratch directory for the current test).
Steps

rows: clicks the element with that text
click-at X Y / move X Y
drags an element by an offset
keyboard input, e.g. key k ctrl
mouse wheel, optionally at a point
advance frames, or wait for animations to finish
some element's whole text equals TEXT
the element, or one of its 3 nearest ancestors, has the class
captures the frame and compares it with baselines/NAME.png

blocks.text: Locators

`click`, `dblclick` and `drag-text` find their target by text. An element whose whole text equals the argument wins (ignoring case and surrounding spaces); only when there is none does the runner fall back to a case-insensitive substring match. In the showroom, `click "color"` therefore opens the color reference page, not background-color or border-color. Use `nth` to pick among several exact matches, counted from 0 in tree order.
Scripts can use the same lookup through the control protocol: `vui-ctl raw '{"cmd":"find","text":"color","exact":true}'` returns `found`, `count`, the element's `rect` and its `text`.
Running and reading the report

blocks.code:
./build/vui-test tests/e2e/showroom.vt
./build/vui-test --out results tests/e2e/*.vt

blocks.text: Each test prints a pass or fail line with its duration; a failing test also prints the step and the reason. The process exits with 1 when anything failed, 2 when a suite cannot be parsed, and 0 otherwise.

The output directory (`vui-test-results` by default) holds `report.html` with every step, its timing and screenshots, `report.json` with the same data for tooling, and `app.log` with the app's stdout and stderr. When a step fails the runner captures `FAIL-<test>.png` of the window at that moment and stops the test.
Baselines

`screenshot NAME` compares the frame with `baselines/NAME.png`. When the baseline does not exist yet it is written and the step passes, so a new test records its own reference on its first run. A mismatch fails the step and writes `diff-<test>--<name>.png`, with differing pixels in red over a gray copy of the frame.

After an intended visual change, rerun with `--update` to rewrite the baselines, review the images in your diff, and commit them. `threshold` absorbs small antialiasing differences; size mismatches always fail.

blocks.code:
./build/vui-test --update tests/e2e/showroom.vt
git diff --stat tests/e2e/baselines

blocks.text: Performance budgets

`expect-frame-ms MAX` waits for the app to settle, reads `frame_ms` from `info` and fails when the last frame took longer than MAX milliseconds. Put it after the steps that build an expensive screen to catch regressions in layout or painting.
Tests render on the software rasterizer, which is several times slower than a GPU. Set budgets from measured sandboxed runs and treat them as regression guards, not as the frame time users see.
Isolation

Every test starts a fresh app process and stops it at the end, the way each Playwright test gets a new browser context. State from one test, such as dark mode or a scrolled page, never leaks into the next.
`{test}` expands to an empty directory created for each test under `<out>/tmp/`. Point the app's data or config at it to start every test from a clean slate:

blocks.code:
app ../bin/notes --data {test}/data
env NOTES_CONFIG={test}/config.toml

blocks.text: The runner owns the `VUI_*` environment. It drops any `VUI_*` variables it inherits and sets `VUI_HIDDEN=1`, the port, size and scale itself, so a stray setting in your shell cannot change how tests run.
The sandbox

Tests are safe to run while you work. On Linux, a headless app (`VUI_HIDDEN=1`) uses SDL's offscreen video driver and Mesa's llvmpipe software rasterizer: it never connects to the compositor, allocates no GPU memory and opens no `/dev/dri` handles. On macOS, where Mesa offscreen GL is unavailable, `VUI_HIDDEN=1` sets `SDL_MAC_BACKGROUND_APP=1` with a hidden Cocoa window rendering offscreen via Metal (or OpenGL fallback) without mapping a window or Dock icon.

The guarantee is checked at two points. On Linux, a headless app refuses to start when the GL renderer it gets is a hardware one, and `vui-test` reads `sandboxed` (or `hidden` on macOS) from `info` and refuses to drive an app that reports false.
`VUI_HIDDEN_GPU=1`, or `vui-test --headed-gpu`, opts into the real GPU on Linux headless runs. Use it only to measure GPU frame times deliberately; it gives up the isolation above.
Continuous integration

CI machines need SDL3 and Mesa's llvmpipe driver, and nothing else: no display server, no GPU, no virtual framebuffer. Build, run the suites, and keep the output directory as an artifact so failures can be inspected from the report.

blocks.code:
# .github/workflows/e2e.yml (steps)
# SDL3 and Odin installed by earlier steps
- run: sudo apt-get install -y libgl1-mesa-dri
- run: ./build.sh
- run: ./build/vui-test --out e2e-results tests/e2e/*.vt
- if: failure()
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with: { name: e2e-results, path: e2e-results }

blocks.text: llvmpipe renders the same pixels for the same input, so baselines recorded locally match on CI when both use the same Mesa release. If they differ, record the baselines on CI with `--update` once and commit them.

docs.title: Styling with utility classes
docs.desc: Build any design by combining single-purpose classes directly in your Odin code.

blocks.text: Build any design by combining single-purpose classes directly in your Odin code.
Each class does one thing: `p-6` sets padding, `rounded-xl` sets the corner radius, `shadow-lg` adds an elevation shadow. You combine them on the element instead of writing a style sheet.
Why it works
Class strings are parsed once and cached, so a frame costs a hash lookup per element, not a parse. Because styling stays next to structure, you can read a component and know exactly how it looks.
Dynamic values
When a value comes from data, build the string with `ui.cx` or set the style directly after the classes are applied with `ui.style()` or `ui.last_style()`.

docs.title: Responsive design
docs.desc: Breakpoint variants adapt a layout to the window width.

blocks.text: Breakpoint variants adapt a layout to the window width.

Breakpoint variants apply from a minimum window width up: `sm` (640px), `md` (768px), `lg` (1024px), `xl` (1280px) and `2xl` (1536px). Use `max-md:` to target widths below a breakpoint. Breakpoints are tokens, so a theme can move them.
Resize the window (or run `vui-ctl resize 700 900`) to watch the card stack vertically below the `md` breakpoint. The showroom itself hides the sidebar below `lg` and the contents rail below `xl`.

docs.title: Dark mode
docs.desc: Style for a dark color scheme with the dark: variant, or with tokens that carry both values.

blocks.text: Style for a dark color scheme with the dark: variant, or with tokens that carry both values.
Prefix utilities with `dark:` to apply them when the app is in dark mode. Toggle it with `ui.set_dark(true)`; the showroom's sun and moon button does exactly that.
Semantic tokens
A token can hold a light and a dark value. The showroom chrome uses tokens such as `bg-canvas`, `text-ink` and `border-rule`, so it needs no `dark:` variants at all.

blocks.code:
ui.theme_set_color(&ctx.theme, "canvas", ui.WHITE, ui.rgb(0x030712))
ui.theme_set_color(&ctx.theme, "ink", ui.rgb(0x030712), ui.WHITE)

// later, anywhere:
ui.text("Title", "text-ink")          // switches with ui.set_dark()

docs.title: Theme tokens
docs.desc: Every utility resolves through a Theme. Change the tokens and the whole app follows, without touching component code.

blocks.text: Every utility resolves through a Theme. Change the tokens and the whole app follows, without touching component code.

The `Theme` struct is the single source of truth: spacing unit, colors, radii, shadows, type scale, weights, tracking, leading, breakpoints, container widths, blur and easing curves. Utilities read from it at parse time; changing a token invalidates the class cache.
Defining tokens in code

blocks.code:
t := &ctx.theme
ui.theme_set_color(t, "brand", ui.rgb(0x7c3aed), ui.rgb(0xa78bfa))
t.radius["card"] = 14
t.spacing = 4                          // p-1 = 4px
ui.theme_changed()

ui.div("rounded-card bg-brand p-6")

blocks.text: Loading a theme file
Themes can live outside the binary. `ui.theme_load_json` merges a JSON file into the current theme, which makes it possible to re-skin a shipped app.
Live token swap
This example changes one token, `accent`, which the whole showroom chrome uses. Watch the sidebar marker and the logo change.

docs.title: Layout engine
docs.desc: How boxes are measured and placed: block flow, flexbox, grid and positioning.

blocks.text: How boxes are measured and placed: block flow, flexbox, grid and positioning.

Layout runs once per frame after the tree is built. Sizes are in logical pixels; the renderer multiplies by the display scale at the very end. The model follows CSS closely enough that Tailwind layouts port without changes.
Box model
Every box is border-box: `w-64 p-4 border-2` is 256px wide in total. Margins never collapse, and `space-x`/`space-y` and `divide-x`/`divide-y` are applied to children by their parent.
Formatting contexts

rows: children stack vertically and stretch; inline-level children flow in lines
single-pass flexbox: basis, grow, shrink, wrap, gap, auto margins, align-content
fr/px/auto tracks, spans, explicit lines, row and column auto-flow
placed against the nearest positioned ancestor or the window
becomes a scroll container with momentum and a draggable scrollbar

blocks.text: Intrinsic sizes

Text reports a min-content width (its longest word) and a max-content width (its unbroken line). Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, so a word never gets crushed. Add `min-w-0` when you want an item to shrink below its content.

docs.desc: Draw charts, meters and dials with vector primitives inside the layout: lines, arcs, curves and gradient fills.

blocks.text: Draw charts, meters and dials with vector primitives inside the layout: lines, arcs, curves and gradient fills.

Utilities cover boxes and text. For charts, meters, dials and anything else that is drawn rather than laid out, use ui.canvas: the element takes part in layout like any other box, and a procedure you supply draws into its rect with vector primitives.
Drawing primitives

rows: box whose content is drawn by draw(ctx, rect, data) every frame
ui.draw_arc(ctx, center, r, start, sweep, color, width)
fill under a curve with a vertical gradient
colors in OKLCH, the same space as Tailwind v4 and modern CSS

blocks.text: Coordinates are logical pixels in window space; the renderer scales them to the display. Every primitive is one GPU instance shaded with a signed distance function, so edges are anti-aliased at any scale and nothing is tessellated on the CPU. A 160-point curve costs 160 instances; a full mixing-desk screen stays around 600.
Frequency response
draw_area fills under the curve with a gradient, draw_polyline strokes it, draw_circle marks the band nodes.

A 270° dial is two arcs and a pointer line. The canvas sits in a normal flex layout with its label underneath.
Live sparklines
Canvases redraw every frame, so they can follow live data. These lines are driven by the clock.
Draw procedures run during painting. Keep them allocation-free or use context.temp_allocator, which is reset after each frame.

docs.title: Game UI
docs.desc: Skeuomorphic HUDs for games: ornate corner shapes, textured materials, orb gauges and inventories, embeddable in a game's own GL context.

blocks.text: Skeuomorphic HUDs for games: ornate corner shapes, textured materials, orb gauges and inventories, embeddable in a game's own GL context.

Games ask for a different register than tools: bevelled metal, carved frames, textured grounds, glowing orbs. vinland-ui draws them with the same one-instance-per-box renderer, so a full RTS console costs a few hundred instances and one draw call per texture, and it can be embedded in a game that owns its own window and GL context (vinland:vui/gl).
What the renderer adds for games

rows: cut, concave or stepped corners; size comes from rounded-*; per corner with corner-tl-*, corner-t-*, ...
pointed arch over the top edge, h is the arch height; half the width gives a round arch
textured fill, multiplied with the background colour or gradient
tile the texture every <px> logical pixels (default: stretch over the box)
procedural tileable textures: hammered, brushed, grain, stone, parchment, weave; masks khatam, interlace, studs
show a texture the game owns (minimap, render target) inside the layout
true when the mouse is over UI: route clicks to the world only when it is false

blocks.text: An RTS command console

The band of an inlaid brass basin: hammered brass rim, bitumen-black field, silver interlace frieze, roundels for the map and the portrait, and command medallions. Click a medallion to arm it: the armed one fills with gold inlay.
Corner shapes
corner-* changes the geometry of a corner and rounded-* its size. Borders, rings, inset shadows and hard shadows follow the shape. Arches take the height of the arch.
Materials

Relief textures are light grey and multiply the background colour or gradient, so one texture serves every metal, wood and stone. Mask textures carry the pattern in alpha: tint them with a colour to inlay a pattern on any ground.
Orb gauges
A health orb is a round frame with a clipped liquid level, a glass highlight on top and a brass ring. The level is a percentage height, so it animates with transition-all.
Inventory and tooltips
Notched slots with rarity rims, a selected slot lit in gold, and a parchment tooltip with scooped corners.
Dialogue under an arch
A pointed arch, a parchment field and an inscriptional face carry the narrative moments; the controls inside stay standard buttons.
Embedding in a game

When a game owns the window, vinland:vui/raylib bridges it: sample input, build the HUD, and render it over the finished world. It draws into the bound framebuffer without clearing it and restores the GL state it touched. Other GL hosts (GLFW, SDL_GL) use vinland:vui/gl directly.

blocks.code:
import ui "vinland:vui"
import vrl "vinland:vui/raylib"

host: vrl.Host
vrl.init(&host, &ctx)                     // after rl.InitWindow
minimap := vrl.texture_image(&host, minimap_tex)

for !rl.WindowShouldClose() {
    if !vrl.pointer_over_ui(&host) { handle_world_clicks() }
    update_world(); update_camera()

    vrl.begin(&host, vrl.input())         // after the camera: labels never lag
    draw_hud()                            // ui.div(...), ui.image(minimap, ...)
    vrl.end(&host)

    rl.BeginDrawing()
    draw_world()
    vrl.render(&host)                     // flushes rlgl, one draw per texture batch
    rl.EndDrawing()
}

blocks.text: Keyboard is left out of vrl.input() by default so game hotkeys (Space, letters) never activate a focused button; pass keyboard = true for menus with text fields.

docs.title: Text rendering
docs.desc: Why text in vinland-ui looks as sharp as in a browser, and the rules the renderer follows.

blocks.text: Why text in vinland-ui looks as sharp as in a browser, and the rules the renderer follows.

Blurry UI text in native apps usually has one of three causes: glyphs rasterized at one size and scaled to another, a window rendered at 1x and stretched by the compositor on a fractional-scale display, or pen positions rounded to whole pixels so spacing wobbles.
What vinland-ui does

rows: SDL3 high-density windows; at 1.333x the framebuffer is 1.333x larger, never stretched
glyphs are rasterized for size × scale, cached per size
4 horizontal phases per glyph keep advances precise
every line sits on a whole physical pixel
rects and border widths round to device pixels so 1px lines stay solid
kern and GPOS pair adjustments from the font
SVG paths go through the glyph rasterizer and atlas
